title.narrative: Provision of life-Saving Nutrition Support for Children Under Five and Pregnant Lactating Mothers in Qansax-dheere

description.narrative: ltpgtADA proposes a 12-month integrated nutrition response targeting seven underserved villages in Qansax Dheere District—Qansaxdhere town, Gedisoy IDP, Duurey, Bandhat, Badbaado, Bulo Guduud, and Shanta Mundule targeting 12,010 beneficiaries. The project addresses persistently high levels of acute malnutrition, micronutrient deficiencies, and suboptimal IYCF practices among vulnerable populations, particularly children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLW). Aligned with Somalia’s national IMAM and MIYCN protocols and Nutrition Cluster priorities, the project integrates curative and preventive interventions. Children aged 6–59 months with uncomplicated SAM will receive treatment at ADA-supported Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP) sites managed by two teams: one based at a static facility and the other delivering services to six outreach sites using a a rented project vehicle. Complicated SAM and MAM cases will be referred to stabilization centers and TSFPs, respectively, managed by partner organizations. ADA will facilitate stabilization center referrals using an ambulance. Cases will be identified through CHW active case finding, family MUAC, three round of mass MUAC screening and inter-program referrals.ltbrgtThe preventive component emphasizes optimal MIYCN practices through a Social and Behavior Change Communication (SBCC) approach anchored mainly on the care group model. Seventy care groups—comprising 56 women and 14 men, each with 12 members—will be formed. Trained Community Health Workers (CHWs) and nutrition workers will conduct household counseling and group education sessions using UNICEF IYCF counseling cards at facilities and in the community, enriched with culturally tailored content. To enhance local food use and diversity, the project will facilitate 70 cooking demonstrations featuring recipes for Tom Brown porridge and spearhead the One Egg Per Child Per Day campaign. To combat micronutrient deficiencies, the project will reach 1,250 children (6–59 months) with Vitamin A supplementation, 850 children with deworming medication, and 850 children (6–23 months) with Micronutrient Powders (MNPs). Additionally, 900 PLW will receive Iron-Folic Acid or Multiple Micronutrient Supplements (MMS), complemented by individualized follow-up and counselling by CHWs. All commodities will be sourced from the Ministry of Health and UNICEF.ltbrgtAn innovative aspect of this intervention is the distribution of conditional, restricted vouchers worth USD 50 to 800 vulnerable households, prioritizing families with children 6–59 months and/or PLW affected by malnutrition, especially those with SAM. Vouchers will be redeemable for two chickens, one tray of eggs, 5kg of chicken feed, and ingredients for Tom Brown porridge (5kg maize flour, 2kg roasted groundnuts, 1.5kg powdered milk, and 1kg sugar). This package is nutritionally calibrated to meet a child’s dietary needs and promote sustained nutrition at the household level. Households will also receive practical training in poultry care and food preparation to ensure proper utilization of the support provided and encourage long-term dietary improvements. Protection mainstreaming will be embedded throughout the project cycle, including training of staff, safe and confidential targeting, establishment of complaints and feedback mechanisms, and prioritized support to high-risk and marginalized groups. 14 community engagement sessions will be held.ltbrgtTo reinforce local ownership and service quality, 26 frontline workers (13 women, 13 men) will be trained on MIYCN, Vitamin A, deworming, and MNP protocols, as well as MIYCN and IMAM. These trainings will be synchronized with other project activities for comprehensive capacity strengthening. Cluster me tools will be used for data collection disaggregated in age, gender and other physiological status. Coordination will be maintained with other cluster partners, state and national cluster and the area based coordination groups.lt/pgt
